still_true: Wegovy's US list price is still $1,349 a month, and almost nobody pays it.
The TrumpRx cash channel still operates, and oral Wegovy starting doses still cost $149 a month there.
The Medicare GLP-1 Bridge pilot has not been revived, Congress has not reopened the ~$41B CBO-scored permanent benefit, and Medicare still pays for no incretin prescribed for weight loss alone.

The September 2027 tri-agency guidance allowing up to 30% premium differentials tied to verified adherence still stands, and Illinois's ban on adherence-conditioned premiums is still the only state ban of that kind in force.
The suicidal-ideation warning is still off the labels.

population.note: FICTIONAL. Cycling arithmetic: 41.0% ever-used − 30.2% current = 10.8% of adults who used and are off now. About 51% of current users are on a second or later course (15.4 points). Many of them are 2033 tariff dropouts and 2034 stoppers who restarted on $39–69 generic semaglutide after January 2036. Another 3.4 points cycled and are off again, so (15.4 + 3.4) / 41.0 ≈ 45.9% of ever-users have cycled. The other ~7.4 points stopped once and have not restarted. This fits one-year persistence near one-third on cash products, ~55% in the shrinking conditioned tracks, and restart rates that rose to ~50% within a year once price stopped being the barrier. Ever-use rose 6.4 points (within the 8.5 cap), mostly from first-time generic starts in the bottom and middle thirds. Age check: 0.20×18.5 + 0.33×31.5 + 0.24×42 + 0.23×26 = 3.7 + 10.4 + 10.1 + 6.0 ≈ 30.2. Income thirds average (34 + 31 + 25.5) / 3 ≈ 30.2. 65+ growth slowed after the April 2035 fracture labelling: new 65+ starts fell ~20% year on year. Users: 30.2% of ~277M adults ≈ 83.7M. FICTIONAL payer mix: commercial ~13.0M (15.5%; ~7.8M on diabetes, CV, OSA or CKD codes and ~5.2M in conditioned weight tracks, down from 9.4M); Medicare ~15.2M (18%); Medicaid ~6.6M (8%; ~1.3M AUD label, the rest diabetes and other codes plus adult weight coverage in 11 states); legitimate cash ~45.9M (55%: ~26.5M generic semaglutide, ~4.0M still on the $149 TrumpRx starting dose, ~15.4M branded direct or TrumpRx, including ~3.1M calm/focus subscribers); imported, compounded or counterfeit ~3.0M (3.6%, down from 5.8M). Sum: 13.0 + 15.2 + 6.6 + 45.9 + 3.0 = 83.7. Generic semaglutide users across payers: 26.5 cash + 4.2 Medicare + 3.8 Medicaid + 2.0 commercial = 36.5M. The ~20% of adults with obesity who have never used a drug shrank to ~15%. They are now concentrated among adults 65+ who were told about fracture risk, uninsured adults without a regular prescriber, and rural counties with no pharmacy. Pediatric: 1.9% of under-18s, ≈ 1.38M of ~73M (12–17 ~4.6% ≈ 1.15M; 6–11 ~0.95% ≈ 0.23M). Growth is suppressed in the 9 states that restrict under-12 prescribing, home to ~21% of children. About 4.6M children live with a parent who regained after stopping, down from 5.3M as parents restarted on generics.

access.public_coverage: Medicare (~15.2M users) still pays only through diabetes, CV, CKD, OSA, dementia-risk (obesity plus established CVD) and AUD codes, behind prior authorisation. Generic semaglutide entered Part D formularies for diabetes and CV codes in Jan 2036. FICTIONAL arithmetic: ~4.2M on generic at ~$30 net plus ~11.0M on brands at ~$215 net gives (4.2×30 + 11.0×215) / 15.2 ≈ $164 average net per month. Then 15.2M × $164 × 12 ≈ $29.9B gross Part D incretin spend, down from ~$38.3B even though users rose. CMS's AUD coding audit (2034) reported in 2035 that ~14% of sampled telehealth AUD diagnoses lacked supporting documentation. CMS issued recoupment letters to two platforms and changed no coverage rule. Medicaid (~6.6M): generic net cost of ~$25–30 a month led four more states (Kentucky, New Mexico, Michigan, Delaware) to add adult weight-loss coverage, generic-only, for 11 in total. AUD coverage continues under existing rebate law. Children 6–11 reach drugs through EPSDT, except where state prescribing restrictions keep a prescription from being written. Two state programmes still condition coverage.
access.generic_rest_of_world: Indian generic semaglutide still sells for $4–30 a month inside India and in 100+ export markets, but the Section 232 100% tariff still shuts Indian finished doses out of the US legitimate channel. Chinese tirzepatide-analogue vials sell for $20–60 where patents are not enforced. Delivered to US addresses they still cost ~$90–180, which is now more than the legal domestic generic. Canadian and Brazilian generics are CAD 40–70 and BRL 140–240. China's Aug 2035 export controls on protected amino acids and synthesis resins raised world API costs ~15–20% for six months before Indian and European reagent makers filled the gap.
access.note: FICTIONAL. Under a March 2035 patent settlement, US generic semaglutide injection (weekly pens and multi-dose vials) launched Jan 2036 from four ANDA holders. One is Keystone Peptide (Lancaster, PA), a DPA Title III-funded domestic producer exempt from the tariff. Cash prices: $39 at warehouse clubs and cost-plus pharmacies for low and mid doses, $49–69 for 2.4 mg maintenance. The generic label carves out the 6–11 indication, which keeps clinical-investigation exclusivity until Feb 2037. Branded prices are unchanged: Wegovy list $1,349, TrumpRx Wegovy pill $149 starting and $199 maintenance, Foundayo $149–229, injectable Wegovy/Zepbound $199–249 direct, MariTide $249. Oral amycretin joined TrumpRx at $299 in Mar 2035 (list $1,299) and has ~8.1M users. Retatrutide is ~$399. No generic oral semaglutide; its settled entry date is 2038. Route mix: generic and branded weekly injectables ~44M (52%), orals ~33.3M (40%), MariTide ~6.4M (8%). The pill stopped being the majority route. Oral parity removed the needle for those who can pay $199–299, while the $49 option is a needle, so the bottom third went back to injecting. Business Group on Health (Nov 2036): 22% of employers cover weight-management use, down from 33%. ~70% of those condition coverage, and unconditional coverage is ~6.5% of employers. Employers that dropped coverage cite 'generic availability at under $70' and fracture-liability concerns. Diabetes and CV codes remain covered almost everywhere, so access now hardens into two tiers: covered or self-paid next-generation pills with DXA and coaching, or cash generic semaglutide with neither. The gray market shrank to ~3.0M: research-grade retatrutide analogues for people chasing triple-agonist efficacy cheaply, counterfeit branded pens, and Mexican border pharmacies used by the uninsured. Domestic re-filling operations largely collapsed once a legal vial cost less than a smuggled one.

drugs.pipeline_note: FICTIONAL. Generic semaglutide injection: Novo settled Paragraph IV litigation on device and formulation patents in Mar 2035. Under the settlement, four ANDA holders entered on 2 Jan 2036, and this realises generic_collapse. Generic oral semaglutide has a settled entry date in 2038. Tirzepatide 6–11 sNDA was filed Feb 2035 and approved Mar 2036 (13 months), with the same growth-monitoring language and a ~0.5 cm/year height-velocity deficit in its trial. Tirzepatide dementia 60+ extension: resubmitted Mar 2035; at the Jan 2036 advisory committee the vote went 9–5 against for women 70+; complete response letter Apr 2036. Bimagrumab label expansion to all incretin users 65+ with low DXA lean-mass index was filed Jun 2035 and was still under review at end 2036 after a three-month extension. It has ~420k users on the restricted label at ~$1,100 list. Oral parity holds at the ~21.5% tier (oral amycretin); no oral matches retatrutide's ~24%. An oral amycretin–bimagrumab co-pack is in phase 2. Implants remain in phase 2 and are not on the market. Global incretin market ~$205B (2035) by value. US branded net revenue fell ~9% in 2036 as semaglutide went generic, while US volume rose ~24%.

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: Still the leading cause of discontinuation. Generic restarters who skipped titration and went straight back to 2.4 mg produced an ED spike in Jan–Mar 2036 that ED networks called 'January nausea'.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Labelled; FDA and pharmacy boards issued re-titration counselling reminders for restarters.

safety_ledger.effect: Gastroparesis, ileus and bowel obstruction (persistent delayed gastric emptying)
safety_ledger.prevalence_note: FICTIONAL: The first two MDL bellwether trials (2035) split: one defence verdict, and one $14M plaintiff verdict on failure to warn about persistence after stopping. GI claims ~44,000. Generic makers are shielded from failure-to-warn suits by federal preemption, so plaintiffs now name brand makers for generic users' injuries under 'innovator liability' theories, which most courts have rejected.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: No new labelling; more bellwethers scheduled for 2037.

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: Elevated with rapid weight loss; unchanged.
No causal confirmation for acute pancreatitis; absolute risk low.

safety_ledger.effect: Lean mass (muscle) loss and bone-density loss
safety_ledger.prevalence_note: FICTIONAL: This is now treated as a population problem. A CMS-FDA Sentinel analysis (Feb 2035) of Medicare users found hip-fracture HR ~1.32 after more than 2 years of use, ~1.5 after three or more cycles, and ~1.6 in women 70+ with BMI below 27 on treatment. Arithmetic: ~16.6M users 65+ × ~3.5 hip fractures per 1,000 person-years baseline (lower than the general 65+ rate because obesity is mildly protective) ≈ 58k expected; an average excess of ~30% gives ≈ 17,000 excess hip fractures a year. At ~20% one-year post-fracture mortality that implies ~3,000 deaths, which CDC has not published and which modellers set against the class's cardiovascular mortality benefit. DXA studies in users under 50 on drug for 5+ years show lean-mass losses of ~8–10% of baseline without resistance training.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Apr 2035 class labelling upgraded fracture and sarcopenia to Warnings and Precautions, recommending baseline DXA at 65+ and after 2 years of use, protein and resistance-training counselling, and caution with rapid titration in older women. CMS issued a national coverage determination for DXA in incretin users 65+ (Oct 2035). The tirzepatide dementia extension was refused (CRL Apr 2036). The bimagrumab expansion is under review.

safety_ledger.effect: Sarcopenic falls and frailty among older cash users without monitoring
safety_ledger.prevalence_note: FICTIONAL: The DXA NCD covers Medicare enrollees, but ~4M users 65+ buy generic semaglutide for cash without a primary-care prescriber, many through telehealth. Medicare Advantage claims show fall-related ED visits rising ~11% among them, against ~5% among monitored users. DXA uptake is ~70% in monitored Medicare users and ~25% among cash generic users 65+.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: FDA medication guide updated for generics. No requirement on telehealth prescribers to order DXA; two state medical boards (Florida, Arizona) issued advisory guidance.

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: Conflicting cohorts; absolute risk very low.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Listed in adverse reactions; no class warning.

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: No new signal in adults, including generic restarters and AUD-label users.

safety_ledger.effect: Reward blunting / emotional flattening ('Ozempic personality', anhedonia)
safety_ledger.prevalence_note: FICTIONAL: Dose-related anhedonia stays at ~7% of maintenance users vs ~3.5% of controls and ~10% on retatrutide. In late 2035 FDA opened a low-dose cohort study through calm-platform records. It has not reported.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: No labelling change. California's and New York's 2035 laws banning mood, focus and calm advertising claims for incretins took effect Jan 2036. No federal enforcement.

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: Half to two-thirds regain within 18 months, worse after repeated cycles. Most 2033 tariff dropouts have now restarted on generics, starting their second or third course with higher fat-to-lean regain ratios.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: None directly; it still underpins conditioned coverage in the remaining tracks.

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: B12, iron, vitamin D and thiamine deficiency (AUD users), plus low ferritin in adolescent girls. Protein insufficiency in older cash users is now linked to the sarcopenia findings.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Annual micronutrient panel language retained, plus protein-intake counselling in the Apr 2035 class update.

safety_ledger.effect: Exocrine pancreatic insufficiency after 5+ years of continuous use
safety_ledger.prevalence_note: FICTIONAL: ~2× EPI incidence after 5+ years of semaglutide; tirzepatide HR ~1.3. EPI claims ~57,000. DOJ settled its civil inquiry with Novo for $1.4B under the False Claims Act (Nov 2035) with no admission.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: EPI wording on semaglutide and tirzepatide labels carries onto the generic labels; Novo's corporate integrity agreement runs through 2040.

safety_ledger.effect: Long-horizon effects beyond ~5 years; effects in children on drug for decades; effects of repeated on/off cycling
safety_ledger.prevalence_note: About fourteen years of semaglutide follow-up now exist. The cycling signal is clearest in bone, where three or more cycles carry HR ~1.5 for hip fracture. There are no data on indefinite starting-dose use.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Pediatric bone and growth postmarketing requirements extended to tirzepatide 6–11.

safety_ledger.effect: Compounded / counterfeit / imported product harms (dosing errors, contamination, substitution)
safety_ledger.prevalence_note: FICTIONAL: Re-filling operations collapsed after legal generics reached $39–49, and the 2034 Burkholderia cluster has not recurred. Harms now concentrate in research-grade retatrutide analogues, with misdosing and one hepatotoxicity cluster in Texas in 2036. Poison-centre calls are ~3.5× 2025 levels, down from ~5×.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Section 232 tariff and Indian export-licence checks remain. FDA warning letters went to research-peptide sellers. No statute changed.

safety_ledger.effect: Growth deceleration, delayed puberty and restrictive eating in children started young
safety_ledger.prevalence_note: FICTIONAL: The liraglutide 6–11 PMR 48-month update still shows height velocity ~0.6 cm/year below expected while on drug, with partial catch-up after stopping. The tirzepatide 6–11 trial deficit is ~0.5 cm/year. Swedish ARFID HR ~1.8. Final adult height is still unknown. Off-label generic semaglutide in under-12s escapes manufacturer PMRs.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Tirzepatide 6–11 approved with monitoring language and no REMS. Nine states restrict under-12 prescribing for weight. AAP kept lifestyle-first for prepubertal children.

safety_ledger.effect: Alcohol-related harms on the AUD label (dehydration, alcoholic ketoacidosis, aspiration with vomiting during binge drinking)
safety_ledger.prevalence_note: FICTIONAL: Postmarketing data confirm ~1 per 2,200 person-years of ketoacidosis or severe dehydration requiring ED care, concentrated in titration.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Titration and hydration warnings strengthened in Warnings and Precautions (2035).

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: FICTIONAL: In early 2036, ~36M people moved to or restarted on generic semaglutide, many switching from daily pills to weekly multi-dose vials. Errors confusing mg doses with syringe units, and people restarting at maintenance dose, drove ~9,000 poison-centre calls in Q1 2036.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: FDA safety communication (Feb 2036); USP labelling standard for multi-dose vials proposed.

food_and_beverage.state: About 47% of US households now have a user. Snack and confectionery volumes are down ~16% from 2025 and sugary drinks ~14%. The 2033 'tariff bounce' in lower-income zips reversed in H1 2036 as generics reached the bottom third, and Dollar General and Family Dollar reported their first sustained snack-volume declines. Kroger's zip-code planning now treats the whole country as 'on-drug', with mini-pack and protein assortments in Memphis as well as Plano. Protein-fortified value lines (store-brand shakes, $1 protein bars) are the growth segment.

alcohol.state: US spirits volumes are down ~20% from 2025 and beer ~14%. Generic semaglutide at $39–49 put drink-less use within reach of heavy drinkers in the bottom third, the volume core of value beer and bottom-shelf spirits. Bardstown-area bourbon cut another ~1,100 jobs, and two craft distilleries in Kentucky closed. Brown-Forman-tier firms pivot to export and to premium low-volume releases. Non-alcoholic and 'calm' drinks reach ~6% of category dollars.

restaurants.state: Traffic is flat to slightly down. QSR value menus that gained in Memphis-type markets in 2034 lost it again in 2036. Chains roll out 'GLP plates' and half portions nationwide. Bar revenue in mid-sized Midwestern cities keeps falling, and Dayton has lost roughly a fifth of its 2030 bar licences.

apparel.state: Plus-size specialists keep shrinking, and Torrid-type chains close ~15% of stores. The size-down wave in lower-income zips lifts resale and stretch denim. Compression and posture garments sold to older women after the fracture news are a small growth line. Structured athletic wear and tailoring keep growing.

fitness.state: Strength training is now near-medical. Medicare Advantage plans added resistance-training benefits after the DXA NCD, and budget gyms (Planet Fitness-type) report record 55+ enrolment. DXA-and-coaching clinics are the premium tier, bundled with bimagrumab and oral amycretin. 'Family strength' programmes keep growing among upper-income parents.

insurance.state: Employer weight coverage fell to 22% as generics gave benefit managers a reason to exit, and conditioned tracks shrank to ~5.2M. Commercial pharmacy trend slowed to ~+3%, the first deceleration in a decade, because covered diabetes and CV claims moved to generic semaglutide. Part D incretin spend fell to ~$29.9B while users rose. Adherence premium differentials survive in the remaining tracks under the 2027 guidance. Medicare Advantage plans fight over who pays for fracture care tied to cash-pay drug use.

pharma.state: Volume up, value split. Novo lost most of its US injectable semaglutide revenue within a year and leans on oral amycretin (~8.1M US users), on its DOJ settlement being behind it, and on ex-US markets. Lilly is steady on tirzepatide, retatrutide and Foundayo, with tirzepatide's own US patent cliff looming. Amgen's MariTide grows inside the shrinking tracks. Keystone Peptide, the DPA-backed domestic generic maker, holds ~22% of US generic semaglutide volume through an HHS purchase commitment for Medicaid and VA. Indian exporters remain locked out of the US but dominate everywhere else.

body_and_culture.what_the_body_signals: Thin no longer signals money; it signals a $49 vial. The body now reads as income through what thinness is made of. Lean with visible muscle, a recent DXA printout and a pill taken at a 6 a.m. window means covered or wealthy: oral amycretin, coaching, sometimes bimagrumab. Thin, soft and stooped with a weekly vial in the fridge means cash generic. In Memphis and the Delta, people who regained in 2034 are thinning again, and neighbours can date who restarted in January.
body_and_culture.thinness_and_class: Muscle and bone density are the class uniform; weight is not. In Buckhead and Plano, 'T-score' is small talk and women in their sixties compare DXA results. In southwest Atlanta and South Memphis, women of the same age use generic semaglutide without a prescriber who orders scans, and the fall and fracture rates are higher there. 'Off-drug lean' persists as the elite boast. Upper-income parents still refuse drugs for prepubertal children. The new marker in children is whether a parent can afford a strength coach instead.
body_and_culture.eating_as_ritual: Shared meals are shorter and drier across the income range now, not only in the suburbs. Church suppers in the Delta changed in 2036 the way country-club dinners changed in 2028. Bread Alone claims ~1,300 congregations and now holds 'full table' suppers with protein-heavy menus and strength classes in fellowship halls. Protein counting has replaced calorie counting as the household arithmetic.
body_and_culture.dating_and_intimacy: App profiles show 'generic' or 'brand' less often than the 2030s jokes predicted, but people read them from photographs anyway. The 'on AUD treatment' tag is common. Older daters in Florida retirement communities ask about bone density before a first hike.
body_and_culture.meaning_of_appetite: With the price gone, appetite stopped being 'the hunger tax' and became a matter of discipline again, now aimed at muscle. The upper tier treats appetite as noise and protein as obligation. The 2034 backlash split. MAHA parents won state laws on children and declared victory. Unmuted turned to the fracture data and older women. Fat-acceptance groups in Oakland argue that the generic made fatness legible as a choice not to pay $49, a stigma worse than before.

interior_life.reward_blunting_prevalence_note: FICTIONAL: Maintenance-dose anhedonia stays at ~7% vs ~3.5% of controls, and ~10% on retatrutide. Calm/focus subscribers rose to ~3.1M (from 2.4M) as platforms moved onto generic semaglutide at $39–49 plus fees, cutting total cost to ~$70–95 a month. About 40% are written on the AUD label. The low-dose anhedonia rate is still unmeasured; FDA's low-dose cohort study opened in late 2035 and has not reported.
interior_life.framing: Platforms sell a feature, but since January 2036 they cannot say so in California or New York. There, 'quiet the noise' became 'craving care' and moved to podcasts and creator sponsorships. Elsewhere the old copy runs. Manufacturers say 'food noise'. HR, where it still pays, calls it steadiness. Clinicians call it dose-related blunting. Unmuted now calls the generic 'sedation at cost price'.
interior_life.effect_on_work: Employer retreat ended weight tracks at many mid-sized firms, but the remaining ~5.2M track enrollees still risk premium tiers on missed logs. EAPs at trucking, warehousing and call-centre employers kept the AUD pill, which is cheaper now. Some switched to paying for generic semaglutide written on the AUD label. FMCSA guidance still covers on-label AUD use and not calm plans. Amazon-scale warehouse operators added mandatory lifting-technique refreshers for workers 55+ after fall claims rose, without saying why. The two EEOC charges remain unresolved.
interior_life.effect_on_art_and_play: 'Off' memoir has given way to 'generic' fiction: novels set in Delta towns in the year everyone restarted. Live-music venues in Columbus and Louisville that lost bar margins now book seated, early shows. Sportsbook handle per account falls in lower-income zips for the first time. Ambient streaming tiers keep marketing to calm subscribers outside the two ad-ban states.
interior_life.effect_on_intimacy: Pill windows structure upper-income mornings, and Sunday vial night structures lower-income weeks. Couples therapists still report the drinking mismatch, now in households that could never have afforded it in 2032. Adult children are now the ones who argue with mothers in their seventies about stopping, because of the fracture labels.
interior_life.effect_on_politics: The backlash finally legislated. Nine states restricted under-12 prescribing for weight, and California and New York banned mood advertising. Federal politics claims the generic. The administration credits Keystone Peptide and the tariff ('the American vial'), while Democrats credit the settlement and Medicaid uptake. In 2036 the 'hunger tax' line disappeared from Delta campaigns. Fracture risk in older women is the new campaign issue in Florida and Arizona. 'Sedated electorate' claims still lack turnout evidence.

state.regulatory_posture: Federal: permissive on approvals (tirzepatide 6–11, generic ANDAs), cautious on older users (fracture class labelling, a CRL for the dementia extension), punitive on imports. States: for the first time, restrictive. Nine states (Tennessee, Utah, Louisiana, Oklahoma, Idaho, Arkansas, South Dakota, Indiana, West Virginia) bar incretin prescribing for weight in under-12s except by a pediatric endocrinologist after six months of documented lifestyle treatment. California and New York ban incretin advertising making mood, focus or calm claims (effective Jan 2036). Illinois's adherence-premium ban is still the only state law of that kind.
state.subsidy_or_mandate: No new federal subsidy. The DPA Title III award (~$1.1B) and an HHS advance purchase commitment for Medicaid and VA volume make Keystone Peptide a de facto national champion. OPM kept FEHB adherence and progress conditions and added generic-first step therapy for 2036. The 2027 tri-agency 30% guidance stands. Four states added generic-only Medicaid weight coverage.
state.conditioning_or_surveillance: Narrower in reach, deeper in the tracks that remain. Track enrolment fell from 9.4M to 5.2M, so fewer people are logged. Inside the tracks, smart-bottle logs, clinic feeds and InBody or DXA scans now flow to wellness vendors, and lean-mass thresholds were added to progress criteria. Cash generic users are mostly unmonitored, which is cheaper and less safe for those over 65. CMS's AUD audit produced recoupments, not new rules. Two state Medicaid programmes still condition coverage.
state.workforce_or_military: TRICARE covers the AUD label and generic semaglutide on diabetes, CV and weight codes for eligible beneficiaries. The Army recruit oral pilot ended in 2035. Recruiters cite stress-fracture concerns in basic training, and recruits on drug must now be off it 90 days before shipping. FMCSA guidance is unchanged.
state.geopolitics_of_supply: The 100% Section 232 tariff on Chinese and Indian peptide drugs and APIs stays. In Aug 2035, after a WTO panel ruled partly in its favour and Washington ignored the ruling, Beijing imposed export controls on protected amino acids and solid-phase synthesis resins. Synthetic generic makers' API costs rose ~15–20% for two quarters and one ANDA launch slipped to March 2036. Commerce then designated peptide API a critical supply chain and funded Keystone Peptide. Novo's Danish and US plants and Lilly's US plants stay exempt. Indian exporters sell to the Gulf, Latin America and Africa, and India's export-licence checks remain.

events.event: Novo Nordisk settles US patent litigation with four generic semaglutide filers, allowing injectable entry on 2 January 2036. The same month it moves oral amycretin onto TrumpRx at $299 a month, giving up the needle to defend the pill.

After a CMS-FDA Sentinel analysis finds hip-fracture risk up about a third in Medicare users on incretins for more than two years, FDA upgrades fracture and sarcopenia to class Warnings and Precautions and recommends DXA scans at 65 and after two years; CMS covers the scans from October

China restricts exports of peptide-synthesis reagents in retaliation for the US tariff; Commerce designates peptide API a critical supply chain and awards $1.1 billion in Defense Production Act funds and an HHS purchase commitment to Keystone Peptide of Lancaster, Pennsylvania

Benefits season: employers covering weight-loss drugs fall from 33% toward 26%, most citing generic availability and fracture liability; by November 2036 the share is 22% and conditioned-track enrolment has fallen from 9.4 million to 5.2 million

Generic semaglutide launches at $39–69 a month cash. About 36 million people are on it by year end, gray-market vial demand collapses, and California's and New York's bans on calm and focus advertising for incretins take effect the same month.
events.driver: price_path: generic_collapse; state_action: restriction; personality_layer: marketed_feature

events.event: FDA approves tirzepatide for children 6–11, while nine states led by Tennessee and Utah have barred incretin prescribing for weight in under-12s since 2035; a Medicaid family in Memphis sues Tennessee, arguing the law conflicts with federal EPSDT coverage

open_tensions: Children under 12 now have three approved drugs, a generic that carves out their indication until February 2037 but is prescribed to them off-label anyway, nine states that forbid prescribing, and a federal Medicaid rule that says medically necessary care must be covered. The Tennessee EPSDT suit will decide which law governs, while final adult height in the first cohorts is still a decade away.

The fracture wave falls hardest on the people generics newly reached: older cash users with no prescriber who orders DXA. The scans, the coaching and bimagrumab sit in the covered and wealthy tier. The CV and dementia benefits that justify the drug in old age now come with ~17,000 excess hip fractures a year, and nobody has netted them officially.

Employer retreat plus a $49 generic turned access into a two-tier system: generic semaglutide at ~15% weight loss for anyone, and 21–24% pills and monthly shots with monitoring for the covered and wealthy. The 2027 adherence-premium guidance still governs the 5.2M left in tracks, and 3.1M calm subscribers take low-dose generic for a feature whose anhedonia rate is still unmeasured.

The cheapest legal vial in America depends on a tariff wall, one DPA-funded plant and reagent supply that Beijing has already shown it can squeeze. Generic oral semaglutide is not due until 2038, and tirzepatide's own patent cliff is approaching.

prose.headline: Thin Is Cheap Now: Semaglutide Hits $49, Thirty Percent of Adults Are On It, and the Rich Have Moved On to Bone
prose.world_in_600_words:
At the end of 2036, three American adults in ten take an incretin drug, about eighty-four million people. More than four in ten have tried one. The number rose because the price fell. On the second of January, under a patent settlement Novo Nordisk signed the previous spring, generic semaglutide went on sale. At a warehouse club a month's starting supply costs thirty-nine dollars, and a maintenance pen costs under seventy. By December about thirty-six million people were using it, many of them for the second or third time.

The return is clearest where the 2033 tariff had pushed people off. In Memphis and the Delta, people who bought Indian vials until the duty tripled their price, and then regained the weight in public, are thinning again, and neighbours can tell who restarted in January. Back-room re-filling operations in Mississippi closed once a legal vial cost less than a smuggled one. The tariff is still in force. The cheapest generic is made in Lancaster, Pennsylvania, by Keystone Peptide, a company Washington funded after Beijing cut off the chemical reagents synthetic peptides need. Officials call it the American vial.

The cheap drug is a weekly needle. The pills that match the injectables, Novo's oral amycretin at two hundred and ninety-nine dollars through TrumpRx and Lilly's Foundayo, belong to people who can pay more or whose insurer still does. Fewer insurers do. Employers looked at a forty-nine-dollar generic and stopped covering weight loss, and only about one in five still pays for it. Most of those require a log, a scan and proof of progress. Diabetes and heart patients are covered almost everywhere. Everyone else pays cash, and what that cash buys depends on income.

The new fault line is bone. In the spring of 2035, federal analysts found that older Medicare patients on these drugs for more than two years broke hips about a third more often. The labels changed and Medicare began paying for bone scans. For people over sixty-five who see a doctor, that means a DXA scan, protein targets and resistance classes, which their Medicare Advantage plans now cover. For the roughly four million who buy the generic online for cash, there is usually no scan. Their fall rates are rising faster. Researchers put the excess at about seventeen thousand hip fractures a year. The government has not weighed that figure against the heart attacks the drugs prevent. In April the FDA declined to extend tirzepatide's dementia claim to healthy older people, citing the fractures in women past seventy.

Because thinness now costs forty-nine dollars, it no longer marks wealth. Muscle and bone density do. In Plano and Buckhead women in their sixties compare T-scores at lunch, while in South Memphis women of the same age are thinner than they have been in years and less steady on stairs.

The states finally acted, mostly over children. Tirzepatide was approved for six-to-eleven-year-olds in March, the third drug for that age. By then nine states, Tennessee first, had barred prescribing for weight to children under twelve without a specialist and six months of documented diet and exercise treatment. A Memphis family on Medicaid is suing, arguing federal children's coverage rules require the drug. California and New York banned ads that sell these drugs as calm, focus or freedom from craving. The platforms renamed their product craving care and moved it to podcasts. Three million people now buy it, mostly on the generic.

The country drinks less, snacks less and pays less for its prescriptions than it did two years ago. The drug now reaches people the tariff priced out, and those who can pay the most are also the ones getting bone scans.
prose.a_day_in_the_life:
Rhonda Pierce takes the vial out of the butter tray at six-fifteen, rolls it between her palms the way the Kroger pharmacist showed her, and draws to the line she marked in Sharpie on the box. Forty-nine dollars. She has written it on the calendar beside JANUARY: BACK ON.

She drives the 240 to Germantown, where Mrs. Ashby, eighty-one, is waiting in the chair by the window with her walker parked like a car. Mrs. Ashby's son pays for the strength coach who comes Tuesdays. Rhonda helps her onto the scale anyway, because the agency sheet asks. Mrs. Ashby asks about the knees. Rhonda says better.

At lunch she eats half a turkey sandwich in the car and puts the other half back in its bag. The church group text says Thursday supper is chicken and beans, protein, bring Tupperware.

After work she picks up Kayla, nine, from her sister's. Kayla's pediatrician said the shot was not something he could write for her in Tennessee. He gave them a pamphlet about the YMCA. Kayla wants to know why Grandma's medicine lives with the butter.

Her mother is at the Baptist rehab off Walnut Grove, six weeks after the hip. The physical therapist says ninety degrees today. Her mother says she is not going back on it, she does not care what the heart doctor says. Rhonda says okay, Mama.

At home she stands on the bathroom scale, steps off, and looks at the kitchen stairs a while before she goes down. On Sunday she will do the vial again.

rationale.badness: Measured against 2026 (3), this world keeps the 2034 harms: EPI litigation, anhedonia at ~7%, child growth deficits and conditioned tracks for ~5.2M.
